items.title: Drag the weights — watch the winner of the RabbitMQ-vs-SQS matrix flip
items.description: L2's decision matrix scored RabbitMQ (41) ahead of SQS (29) using message-size fit weighted at 4 and operational cost weighted at 3 — the option scores themselves (1-5 per criterion) stay fixed, exactly as in that table. Drag either weight and watch the total for each option, and the gap between them, change in real time.
items.compute: const familiarityWeight = 2; const lockInWeight = 1; const sqsScores = { sizeFit: 2, cost: 5, familiarity: 2, lockIn: 2 }; const rabbitScores = { sizeFit: 5, cost: 2, familiarity: 5, lockIn: 5 }; const sqsTotal = params.sizeFitWeight * sqsScores.sizeFit + params.costWeight * sqsScores.cost + familiarityWeight * sqsScores.familiarity + lockInWeight * sqsScores.lockIn; const rabbitTotal = params.sizeFitWeight * rabbitScores.sizeFit + params.costWeight * rabbitScores.cost + familiarityWeight * rabbitScores.familiarity + lockInWeight * rabbitScores.lockIn; return { sqsTotal, rabbitTotal };

items.title: How often does an ADR need reviewing to keep stale ones from piling up?
items.description: A team accepts roughly 12 significant decisions a year. On average, about 1 in 4 accepted decisions stops reflecting reality within 18 months (a vendor changes, a constraint disappears) unless someone catches it and writes a superseding ADR. Drag how often the team actually runs the stale-ADR review (like L3's flagger script) and see how many accepted ADRs are silently wrong at any given moment, the way ADR-014 was in the L3 Scenario.
items.compute: const adrsAcceptedPerYear = 12; const staleFractionPer18Months = 0.25; const monthsToGoStale = 18; const staleRatePerMonth = staleFractionPer18Months / monthsToGoStale; const activeAdrs = adrsAcceptedPerYear * 2; const silentlyStaleAdrs = Math.round(activeAdrs * staleRatePerMonth * Math.min(params.reviewIntervalMonths, monthsToGoStale * 2)); return { silentlyStaleAdrs };

outputs.label: Accepted ADRs currently wrong and undetected
